Looking at the demo: the 15x15 input becomes 30x30, tiled as four quadrants — top-left is the input itself, top-right is its 90° clockwise rotation, bottom-left is its 90° counter-clockwise rotation, and bottom-right is its 180° rotation (verified against many rows of the demo output).

```python
def transform(grid):
    n = len(grid)
    cw = [list(row) for row in zip(*grid[::-1])]          # rotate 90 clockwise
    ccw = [list(row) for row in zip(*[r[::-1] for r in grid])][::-1]  # rotate 90 ccw
    r180 = [r[::-1] for r in grid[::-1]]                  # rotate 180
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        out.append(list(grid[i]) + list(ccw[i]))
    for i in range(n):
        out.append(list(cw[i]) + list(r180[i]))
    return out
```

The top-right and bottom-left quadrants were swapped: top-right is the clockwise rotation, bottom-left is counter-clockwise. Corrected:

```python
def transform(grid):
    n = len(grid)
    cw = [list(r) for r in zip(*grid[::-1])]   # rotate 90 CW
    ccw = [list(r) for r in zip(*grid)][::-1]  # rotate 90 CCW
    r180 = [r[::-1] for r in grid[::-1]]       # rotate 180
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        out.append(list(grid[i]) + cw[i])
    for i in range(n):
        out.append(ccw[i] + r180[i])
    return out
```
